lines.text: The LORD tells Moses to warn Pharaoh of swarms of flies, but Goshen, where His people live, will have none.
Flies ruin Egypt, and Moses refuses to sacrifice in the land, saying they must go a three-day journey into the wilderness.
Pharaoh tells them not to go very far, and when Moses prays, the LORD removes the flies, but Pharaoh hardens his heart.
The LORD sends a plague on Egypt's livestock, including horses, donkeys, sheep, herds, and flocks, but none of Israel's animals die.
Moses tosses soot from the furnace into the air, and festering boils break out on man and beast, so the magicians cannot stand before Moses.
